newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ROBSON LAMENTS TIMING OF NEWCASTLE VACANCY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON LAMENTS TIMING OF NEWCASTLE VACANCY.

text.p: Barcelona coach Bobby Robson hinted on Saturday he would have liked to take over from Kevin Keegan as manager of Newcastle if the timing had been better.

"When I came (to Barcelona) in August it was what I have wanted for 18 years, and now I have taken it," said the former England coach, who repeated his intention to stay with the Spanish giants for the time being. "And five months later I get the opportunity to go home where my head and heart is. It's just come at the wrong time in a way. It's sod's law."
Speaking to the BBC from Camp Nou four days after Keegan's dramatic departure from St James's Park, Robson appeared distracted when asked about his plans for the future.

"I've no idea. My mind is made up," he said. "There is no greater pleasure than to go there at the right time with all things in perfect position but it isn't like that. I am at this club and I want to bring success to this club which they haven't had for two years."

Robson has 18 months left on his contract at Barcelona but has come under increasing pressure from their demanding fans in recent weeks, despite guiding the Catalan side to second place in the Spanish league just two points behind Real Madrid.

He originally comes from the north-east of England and has been linked with a return to his home region ever since Keegan quit, but both Robson and Barcelona have repeatedly denied he is about to leave Camp Nou.
"I am at this club and I want to bring success to this club which they haven't had for two years," he told the BBC.
